narrative: OMX30 opens into a mixed but structurally constructive session. Continental strength (DAX, CAC both +0.75%+) and a mild positive correlation signal (+0.278%) provide tailwind, while the USD/SEK spike to 9.62 (+1.02%) is a material positive for Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson. The index sits firmly in bull regime (+8.9% above 200-MA) with MACD bullish, but the overbought Stochastic (K=86.7, D=84.9) and RSI at 58 hint at near-term consolidation rather than acceleration. Copper's +1.15% bounce is constructive for Boliden; oil's -1.74% slide eases industrial margin concerns. US 10Y yield +1.16% (4.726%) widens bank NIM but pressures tech DCF valuations. Key risk: Gita Gopinath's protectionism warning and UK budget uncertainty could trigger volatility.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to open +0.3% to +0.5% on Continental leadership and strong USD/SEK (9.62, +1.02%). Watch the 3123 pivot (yesterday close); resistance at 3180 (50-MA) and support at 3085 (lower Bollinger). Stochastic deep in overbought (K=86.7, D=84.9)—watch for profit-taking if we rally into the session. Sectors: Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) POSITIVE on yield lift (4.726% +1.16%); Industrials (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A) POSITIVE on USD/SEK strength; Tech/Telecom (Ericsson B, Hexagon B) MIXED (NASDAQ -0.50% headwind, but exporter USD benefit); Mining (Boliden) POSITIVE on copper +1.15%. Consumer/Retail (H&M B) watch for margin pressure (weak EUR/SEK, oil down but sourcing costs via weak EUR matter more). Real Estate likely soft (yields rising, refinancing costs up). US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—monitor for recession signals. Top risk: trade rhetoric escalation (Gopinath comments) could spike VIX (14.63) and reverse rally.
